newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis against fixed figure in EU stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis against fixed figure in EU stability pact.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday it would be very unwise to use a fixed figure to define the temporary and exceptional circumstances that would exempt countries from sanctions under a proposed European Union budget stability pact.
EU finance ministers failed to agree on Monday on the terms of a stability pact after Germany insisted that temporary and exceptional circumstances must be quantified.
Arthuis, speaking at a conference on the euro, noted that he had said on Monday he was not convinced these exceptional circumstances could be quantified.
"Quantification poses problems," Arthuis said, adding that the size and effect of an economic recession could vary from one country to another.
Small countries could reach high levels of budget deficits very quickly, while the process would be slower for big countries, he said.
"It is very unwise to fix one single figure for everybody," he said.
Arthuis noted that Germany wanted to define temporary and exceptional circumstances as being an economic shrinkage of two percent or more.
"Since the Liberation (end of World War Two), France has never had such a recession," he said.
EU member states would have to narrow their differences to reach a compromise, he said.
Germany has proposed a budget stability pact which would prevent members of European monetary union from running up big deficits after the creation of the euro.

Countries which ran budget deficits of more than three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) would be subject to fines unless they could show that the overshoot was due to temporary and exceptional circumstances.
